text:
sara_support: escalating ticket INC-4821 — customer reported an overnight bulk embeddings job started getting large numbers of 429s after ~35m of running. they sent a few snippets, said they already implemented exponential backoff, but hits keep coming. ticket: https://zendesk.example/INC-4821 :exclamation:

ben_cs: pasted customer summary from call — they batch 100 inputs per request and run ~20 concurrent workers. job peak ~2.2k requests/minute. they see 429s with Retry-After between 60-180s. customer also mentioned an earlier 'dimension mismatch' error once, but that was fixed by upgrading the client lib. main issue now is sustained 429 spikes on embeddings endpoint.

kai_oncall: copying logs from k8s ingress. noticed a sharp cut at ~00:34UTC then steady 429s. ingress returned: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2025 00:34:15 GMT
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 35
retry-after: 120
```
Request ids: req-7f8b2a6c, req-7f8b2b0d, req-7f8b2f99. throwing to eng-platform for rate-limit policy check.

maria_ml: quick notes from model side — embeddings models are CPU/GPU-bound by vector encode time. we allow per-customer concurrency + global burst window. if they run 2.2k req/min that's ~36 rps sustained which may exceed per-minute quota depending on their tier and recent quota uses. also batching 100 per request increases per-request processing time and might trigger longer running requests that count towards concurrent request limits. recommend they use server-side bulk endpoint (batching at 512 items per job) or reduce concurrency and add randomized jitter to backoff.

lee_platform: I checked rate limiter config for the embeddings route for this org id. they are on default quota: 60 requests/min per API key, with a short burst allowance of +30 for 10s. their traffic pattern exceeded both. we also have a global protection that temporarily reduces burst if node CPU > 75% across cluster to protect latency SLOs — saw that at the same time. two actionable items: 1) request temporary quota bump for them from Accounts if they need sustained throughput; 2) suggest they switch to our bulk ingestion job via POST /v1/embeddings/bulk which is rate-limited differently (higher per-job token cap).

ben_cs: customer logs show they did exponential backoff but with fixed base and no jitter, so thundering herd after backoff may re-hit bucket causing cascading 429s. they tried reducing workers to 6 and still saw intermittent 429s. want to share recommended client pattern and a repro curl.

ticket-bot: ticket INC-4821 updated: assigned to maria_ml, lee_platform; priority P1 -> P2 if quota bump approved.

maria_ml: repro curl for their exact pattern (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {{KEY}}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["... 100 items ..."]}'
```
Response example: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 120
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "quota exceeded for key" }
```
Suggested client backoff pseudocode: 
```
backoff = jittered_exponential(base=200ms, cap=30s)
for attempt in 0..N:
  resp = do_request()
  if resp.status == 429:
    sleep(backoff())
    continue
  else:
    break
```
Use full jitter (random between 0..base*2^n) and cap. Also limit concurrency on client side to recommended <= 8 for their worker VM size.

kai_oncall: forensics: CPU spike on embeddings pool correlated with lockout start; platform reduced burst window at 00:33:50 to protect SLO. we've captured node-level metrics and saved to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-4821/metrics.tar.gz.

lee_platform: next steps from platform side: submitted internal quota adjustment request to accounts (req-acc-993). if approved we can raise per-minute quota to 600 for 24h for them while they re-architect. also can enable a temporary soft-throttle that will queue requests for up to 10s instead of returning 429 for low-priority traffic — need approvals.

ben_cs: action items for CS/Customer: 1) implement full-jitter backoff and decrease worker concurrency by 50% tonight; 2) switch to bulk ingestion endpoint for next run; 3) share new run logs (req ids) if still hitting 429s. I'll send a quick how-to and example repo.

maria_ml: note — double-check that they aren't mixing model IDs in parallel jobs (one engine returns 1,536-d vectors vs another 3,072-d config); mixing can surface as downstream dimension mismatch when they try to concatenate outputs into a single matrix. that was the earlier error but not the 429 root cause.

sara_support: I'll update the ticket with the above and ask customer to run a small staged test (10 requests at 2s interval, then ramp) and send request ids. assigned to maria_ml and lee_platform. follow-up scheduled in 2h. :thumbsup:

ben_cs: customer replied in thread: "thanks — we'll implement jitter + drop concurrency and rerun the job tonight. if you can push a temporary quota increase please let us know asap."

kai_oncall: leaving traces and links in ticket: logs, metrics, and ingress traces. if we see 429s after client-side changes, we'll create a postmortem.

lee_platform: ack. will update when accounts responds to req-acc-993.

sara_support: closing loop here for now. will ping if anything new.
